questions.hint: Set Qd equal to Qs and solve.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: In an engineer's design brief, the price of a complement falls; what happens to demand for this good?

options.text: Demand shifts left because complement is cheaper
Supply shifts right because firms expand
Demand shifts right because total cost falls
No change because own price fixed

questions.explanation: A lower complement price raises demand for this good, shifting right. Buyers face lower total cost.
questions.hint: Complement price down means demand up.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: In an engineer's design brief for a valve, a per-unit tax is imposed on producers; explain the supply shift.

answer.exemplar: A per-unit tax raises production cost, so firms offer less at each price and supply shifts to the left.

questions.explanation: Taxes on producers raise marginal cost and reduce supply. The curve shifts left.
questions.hint: Tax on producers shifts supply left.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: In an engineer's design brief, price sits below equilibrium; the data show Qd greater than Qs. What adjustment follows?

options.text: Surplus builds and price falls
Supply shifts right automatically
No change because price is low
Shortage builds and price rises toward equilibrium

questions.explanation: Below equilibrium, demand exceeds supply, creating shortage that raises price. Surplus would occur above.

questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.stem: In an engineer's design brief, demand rises and supply rises; the data show both curves shifting right. What is the effect on equilibrium quantity?

options.text: Quantity rises because both shifts push quantity up
Quantity is indeterminate
Quantity falls because effects cancel
Quantity doubles because both shift

questions.explanation: Both shifts raise quantity, so quantity rises. Price change is ambiguous.
